body.statement: Theorem 3. For \(J=2\) and \(s=1\), the rational certificate \((q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U},\pi^{\mathrm H})\) satisfies \(q^{\mathrm U}\notin\mathcal C_2\) and \[\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{2,1}}\mathcal R_h(q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})<9065/100000.\] Its displayed dual prior satisfies \[\min\left\{B_{(0,0,2)}(\pi^{\mathrm H}),\sum_{n\in\mathcal N_2}q^{\mathrm{Ber}}_nB_n(\pi^{\mathrm H})\right\}>9102/100000,\] and therefore \(\inf_{q'\in\mathcal C_2,\,\eta'}\max_h\mathcal R_h(q',\eta')>0.09102\). Hence \(\mathcal Q^*(2,1)\cap\mathcal C_2=\varnothing\), with an all-estimator risk gap exceeding \(37/100000\).
body.justification: A strict rational separation prevents the intermediate problem from collapsing to an endpoint switch or a paired--Bernoulli mixture.
body.gap: Kallus2021Optimality shows mixed strategies can matter for fixed-estimator variance, but no published result gives a strict noncanonical separation after optimizing every measurable SATE estimator.
body.consumer: For sensitivity analysis at \(J=2,s=1\), the result shows that restricting attention to mixtures of paired and independent assignment can be strictly suboptimal even after reoptimizing the estimator.
